title: Density is not the energy of the whole packet
question: Why does a finite light complex need a volume calculation?
recap: In the new frame the light’s energy density changes by the factor q squared, while the volume of the same light complex, measured at one instant of the new time, changes by 1/q. Its total energy therefore changes by q, the same factor as its frequency.
premises: Compare the same finite light complex on each frame’s own simultaneous slice.
Use the plane-wave field transformation with q defined from the unprimed direction.
limitations: A light complex is not a material rod or a photon rest frame.
The energy law does not need the light-quantum hypothesis or the desired mass-energy conclusion.

overview.text: In the new frame the light’s energy density changes by the factor \(q^2\), while the volume of the same light complex, measured at one instant of the new time, changes by \(1/q\). Its total energy therefore changes by \(q\), the same factor as its frequency.

full.spoken: Energy density scales by q squared, packet volume by inverse q, and total energy by q.

full.text: Einstein bounds the light complex by a sphere that moves with the light. That boundary is not a body at rest in either frame, so the ordinary contraction of a material body does not apply to it. At \(0.6c\), for light travelling the same way as the observer, \(q = 0.5\): the density falls to one quarter, the volume doubles, and the total energy halves.

Treating the light complex as a body at rest in the original frame, and shrinking its volume by \(1/\gamma = 0.8\), would give a total-energy factor of \(0.25 \times 0.8 = 0.2\) instead of 0.5. For light crossing the motion at right angles in the original frame the two volume factors happen to agree, both 0.8, so that case alone cannot catch the mistake. The light-packet laboratory includes the case that tells them apart.
The mass-energy paper of September 1905 starts from exactly this transformation of light energy. It does not assume \(E = mc^2\) in advance, and it needs no localized light quanta.

full.returnCaption: Return to why does a finite light complex need a volume calculation.

items: Transform the wave’s amplitude. The energy density goes as its square, so it changes by \(q^2\).
Draw a boundary around the light complex: a sphere that moves with the light.
Find the region that moving boundary encloses at one instant of the new time \(t'\).
Its volume is \(1/q\) times the original volume.
Multiply density by volume: \(q^2 \times 1/q = q\). The total energy changes by \(q\), the same factor as the frequency, and not by \(q^2\).
Check the case along the motion at \(0.6c\): 0.5 with the correct volume, and 0.2 if the volume is shrunk like a material body’s.

margin.text: Here \(u\) is energy density and \(V_{\mathrm{packet}}\) the volume of the complex. The letter \(L\) is avoided: in this paper it names a magnetic component, and in the mass-energy paper the emitted energy. The calculation follows one bounded complex of light; it gives light no rest frame.
